title: FACT CHECK: Trump didn’t issue an arrest warrant against Marcos
summary: No credible report confirms the existence of a supposed warrant, and the video offers no evidence to back up its claim

blocks.text: Claim: US President Donald Trump has issued an arrest warrant against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., who is now “wanted among world leaders.”

Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube video was posted by the channel “News Update Files” on November 15, as the Philippines began hosting the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit. It is titled, “Ngayon lang! Trump naglabas ng arrest warrant kay Bangag?! Wanted na si Bangag sa mga world leaders?!”
(Just now! Trump issues an arrest warrant against Bangag?! Is Bangag now wanted by world leaders?!)
Its thumbnail shows photos of Marcos and of Trump holding a document stamped “ARREST WARRANT.” Text overlaid on it reads, “Bangag kulong na?! Trump naglabas ng warrant! Buti nga sa’yo! Bangag ka!”
(Will Bangag be jailed?! Trump issues a warrant! Serves you right! You’re high!)
Another photo used in the video includes the text, “ASEAN Summit [canceled]?!”
As of writing, the video has 32,000 views and 3,100 likes.
The facts: No credible media report, US government statement, or court record shows Trump issuing an arrest warrant against Marcos.
The video does not present proof for its claim either. Its content is merely commentary criticizing the Philippines’ hosting of the summit and alleging mismanagement and poor foreign relations.
Additionally, Marcos cannot be arrested while he is president, as he enjoys immunity from suit.

The video surfaced as Trump arrived in Manila on November 17 for a state visit and to participate in the ASEAN-US Special Summit and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue leaders’ summit. On November 18, Marcos welcomed Trump in Malacañang for bilateral talks and a state luncheon.

Trump opened the meeting by calling the Philippines one of America’s oldest and most important alliances in the Pacific, describing it as “a bond formed in blood.” He said the US is expanding its defense cooperation with the Philippines.

At the luncheon, Trump announced “the biggest trade deal we’ve ever made by far,” without giving details. Malacañang described it more as “an understanding on economic cooperation, particularly food and energy supply,” and later said that no deal was signed, including the controversial Pax Silica agreement.

The video’s claim about a canceled ASEAN summit is also unfounded. The summit went ahead and wrapped up on November 17, closing the Philippines’ year-long chairmanship of the regional bloc. (READ: ‘Successful’ ASEAN Summit ends with Marcos unable to solve its hardest problems).
Trump’s return: Trump returned to the Philippines after nine years, having last visited in November 2017.
Following his Manila stop, he is now in China for a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Meanwhile, Marcos is also in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.
